tests.title: find_references is registered in tools.All() following find_symbol and in FileNavigationTools() with correct metadata
given: a tool set created with default options and workspace
tests.when: tools.All() and tools.FileNavigationTools() are inspected
then: tools.All() contains find_references immediately following find_symbol and preceding shell tools
tools.FileNavigationTools() contains exactly six tools including find_references
find_references has Builtin set to true and ExecutionMode set to core.Parallel
find_references is not present in guard.ShellToolNames
find_references prompt guidelines contain 'Use find_symbol for where a name is declared, find_references for who uses it, and search_files for text.'
tests.pseudocode: all, err := tools.All(opts); idxFS := indexOf(all, "find_symbol"); idxFR := indexOf(all, "find_references"); assert idxFR == idxFS + 1; nav := tools.FileNavigationTools(); assert len(nav) == 6 && contains(nav, "find_references"); fr := all[idxFR]; assert fr.Builtin && fr.ExecutionMode == core.Parallel && !guard.ShellToolNames[fr.Name]; assert contains(fr.PromptGuidelines, "Use find_symbol for where a name is declared, find_references for who uses it, and search_files for text.")

tests.title: find_references input schema specifies required name and optional path, kind, include_tests, and max_results
given: the find_references tool definition from tools.All()
tests.when: InputSchema is inspected against schema rules
then: InputSchema is an Object schema
property 'name' is required and of type string
properties 'path', 'kind', 'include_tests', and 'max_results' are optional
property 'include_tests' is of type boolean
property 'max_results' is of type integer
tests.pseudocode: fr := getTool("find_references"); schema := fr.InputSchema; assert schema.IsRequired("name"); assert schema.PropertyList()["name"].Type == schema.TypeString; assert schema.PropertyList()["include_tests"].Type == schema.TypeBoolean; assert schema.PropertyList()["max_results"].Type == schema.TypeInteger

tests.title: find_references rejects malformed JSON, empty name, whitespace name, or name exceeding 256 bytes
given: a workspace and initialized fileTools
tests.when: find_references is executed with malformed JSON, missing name, empty string name, whitespace name, and a 257-byte name
then: each invocation returns ToolResult with OK false
error code is 'invalid_arguments'
error message is non-empty explaining the validation failure
no filesystem reads or symbol table queries are performed
tests.pseudocode: for in := range []string{"{bad-json", "{}", "{\"name\":\"\"}", "{\"name\":\"   \"}", "{\"name\":\"" + strings.Repeat("a", 257) + "\"}"} { res := fr.Execute(ctx, []byte(in)); assert !res.OK && res.Error == "invalid_arguments" && res.Text != "" }

tests.title: find_references rejects invalid kind parameters with a list of valid kinds
given: a workspace and initialized fileTools
tests.when: find_references is executed with kind 'struct', 'unknown', or 'class_method'
then: each invocation returns ToolResult with OK false
error code is 'invalid_arguments'
error message lists valid kinds: func, method, type, class, interface, enum, trait, const, var, module, macro
tests.pseudocode: res := fr.Execute(ctx, []byte(`{"name":"Foo","kind":"struct"}`)); assert !res.OK && res.Error == "invalid_arguments"; for _, k := range validKinds { assert strings.Contains(res.Text, k) }

tests.title: find_references refuses a path resolving outside workspace root
given: a workspace with a temporary directory root
tests.when: find_references is executed with path '../outside' or an absolute outside path
then: each invocation returns ToolResult with OK false
error code is 'path_not_allowed'
workspace directory is not inspected
tests.pseudocode: res := fr.Execute(ctx, []byte(`{"name":"Foo","path":"../outside"}`)); assert !res.OK && res.Error == "path_not_allowed"

tests.title: find_references rejects non-existent paths or paths pointing to regular files
given: a workspace containing a regular file 'main.go' and no directory named 'missing_dir'
tests.when: find_references is executed with path 'missing_dir' and with path 'main.go'
then: both invocations return ToolResult with OK false
error code is 'invalid_arguments'
error message indicates the directory was not found or is not a directory
tests.pseudocode: res1 := fr.Execute(ctx, []byte(`{"name":"Foo","path":"missing_dir"}`)); assert !res1.OK && res1.Error == "invalid_arguments" && strings.Contains(res1.Text, "directory"); res2 := fr.Execute(ctx, []byte(`{"name":"Foo","path":"main.go"}`)); assert !res2.OK && res2.Error == "invalid_arguments"

tests.title: find_references terminates immediately with aborted error when context is cancelled
given: a workspace with source files and an already cancelled context
tests.when: find_references is executed with cancelled context
then: ToolResult has OK false
error code is 'aborted'
error message equals 'Operation aborted'
tests.pseudocode: ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background()); cancel(); res := fr.Execute(ctx, []byte(`{"name":"Foo"}`)); assert !res.OK && res.Error == "aborted" && res.Text == "Operation aborted"

tests.title: Declaration resolver queries shared symbol table for unqualified and container-qualified names
given: a workspace containing type Runner with method Run, and a standalone function Run
tests.when: declaration resolver searches for unqualified 'Run' and container-qualified 'Runner.Run'
then: query for 'Run' matches both declarations
query for 'Runner.Run' matches only the member Run on container Runner
tests.pseudocode: matches := resolveSymbolCandidates(st, "Run", "", ""); assert len(matches) == 2; m2 := resolveSymbolCandidates(st, "Runner.Run", "", ""); assert len(m2) == 1 && m2[0].Container == "Runner" && m2[0].Name == "Run"

tests.title: Declaration resolver filters candidate declarations by kind and path constraints
given: a workspace containing a type Config in 'pkg/config.go' and a function Config in 'pkg/setup.go' and a type Config in 'cmd/main.go'
tests.when: declaration resolver queries name 'Config' with kind 'type' and path 'pkg'
then: candidates in 'cmd/' are excluded by directory scope
candidates with kind 'func' are excluded by kind filter
only the type Config in 'pkg/config.go' remains
tests.pseudocode: matches := resolveSymbolCandidates(st, "Config", "type", "pkg"); assert len(matches) == 1 && matches[0].Path == "pkg/config.go" && matches[0].Kind == "type"

tests.title: Declaration resolver selects the highest-ranked candidate applying find_symbol precedence
given: a symbol table containing multiple candidates matching 'Handle': unexported 'handle' in test file, unexported 'handle' in 'a.go', exported 'Handle' in 'test/handle_test.go', and exported 'Handle' in 'pkg/handle.go'
tests.when: declaration resolver disambiguates the candidate set
then: exact name match 'Handle' is prioritized over prefix or case-variant matches
exported declaration is prioritized over unexported
non-test file declaration is prioritized over test file
shorter path and earlier line break ties deterministically
top-ranked candidate is exported 'Handle' in 'pkg/handle.go'
tests.pseudocode: target := disambiguateSymbol(candidates); assert target.Path == "pkg/handle.go" && target.Name == "Handle"

tests.title: Declaration resolver falls back to text search with zero target declaration when name is not found
given: a workspace containing files mentioning string 'GOPHER_KEY' but no declaration in symbol table
tests.when: find_references is executed for 'GOPHER_KEY'
then: ToolResult has OK true
target in structured Data is zero outline.Decl
backend is 'text'
text header indicates zero declarations matched and shows text references count
tests.pseudocode: res := fr.Execute(ctx, []byte(`{"name":"GOPHER_KEY"}`)); assert res.OK; data := res.Data.(ReferenceResult); assert data.Target == outline.Decl{} && data.Backend == "text"; assert strings.Contains(res.Text, "0 references") || strings.Contains(res.Text, "text matches")

tests.title: Qualified declaration name splitting matches member and container across arbitrary dot-separated identifiers
given: an in-memory symbol table populated with nested types and containers
tests.when: for any qualified declaration name formatted as Container.Member, the name is split at the last dot
then: the container prefix equals all characters before the last dot
the member name equals all characters after the last dot
matched symbol declarations have Container matching container prefix and Name matching member name
tests.pseudocode: for name in genQualifiedNames() { container, member := splitContainerMember(name); match := matchContainerSymbol(st, container, member); if match != nil { assert match.Container == container && match.Name == member } }

tests.title: Go type resolver parses workspace packages and type-checks with workspace-local importer without external processes
given: a Go workspace with root go.mod defining module 'example.com/mod' and subpackages 'pkg/a' and 'pkg/b' importing 'pkg/a'
tests.when: Go type resolver checks package 'pkg/b'
then: import of 'example.com/mod/pkg/a' resolves to local sources in 'pkg/a'
types in 'pkg/a' are fully resolved in 'pkg/b'
no external shell commands or network connections are invoked
tests.pseudocode: imp := newWorkspaceImporter(ws, "example.com/mod"); pkg, err := checkPackage(imp, "pkg/b"); assert err == nil && pkg != nil; assert pkg.Imports()[0].Path() == "example.com/mod/pkg/a"

tests.title: Go type resolver stubs external imports with empty synthetic packages and FakeImportC without aborting
given: a Go source file importing standard library 'fmt', 'os' and external 'github.com/stretchr/testify/assert' and 'C'
tests.when: Go type resolver type-checks the package
then: types.Config.FakeImportC is true
importer returns synthetic empty *types.Package for 'fmt', 'os', and external dependencies
type checking completes without panicking or returning fatal process aborts
collected type errors are recorded in result error count
tests.pseudocode: cfg := makeTypesConfig(importer); pkg, errs := typeCheck(cfg, parsedFiles); assert pkg != nil; assert importer.imported["fmt"].Scope().Len() == 0; assert len(errs) > 0

tests.title: Go type resolver attributes resolved confidence to receiver method calls, interfaces, renamed imports, and promoted fields
given: a Go workspace with interface Reader, struct Buffer implementing Reader, renamed package import 'alias', and embedded struct Base with method Ping
tests.when: reference resolution is performed for Ping, Read, and alias function calls
then: receiver method calls 'buf.Ping()' through embedded Base resolve with confidence 'resolved'
interface method invocations 'r.Read()' resolve with confidence 'resolved'
calls through renamed package import 'alias.Do()' resolve with confidence 'resolved'
tests.pseudocode: sites := resolveGoReferences(targetPing); assert len(sites) > 0; for _, s := range sites { assert s.Confidence == "resolved" }

tests.title: Go type resolver excludes same-named methods on unrelated types or distinct packages
given: a Go workspace with type Alpha defining method Close() and type Beta defining method Close() in another package
tests.when: find_references resolves references for Alpha.Close
then: calls to 'beta.Close()' are excluded from the reference results
only calls whose receiver resolves to Alpha's Close method are included
tests.pseudocode: sites := resolveGoReferences(alphaClose); for _, s := range sites { assert s.Path == "alpha_caller.go" && !strings.Contains(s.Source, "beta.Close") }

tests.title: Go type resolver demotes incompletely typed identifiers to lexical confidence instead of dropping them
given: a Go function receiving an interface from stubbed external package 'external.Client' calling 'client.Do()' where 'Do' matches target declaration
tests.when: find_references resolves references for target 'Do'
then: the call site 'client.Do()' is not omitted
the reference site is assigned confidence 'lexical'
tests.pseudocode: sites := resolveGoReferences(targetDo); hit := findSite(sites, "client.Do()"); assert hit != nil && hit.Confidence == "lexical"

tests.title: Go source parsing preserves comments and records 1-based line and column offsets via token.FileSet
given: a workspace containing arbitrary valid Go source files
tests.when: for any Go package in the workspace, source files are parsed with comments enabled
then: the parsed ast.File includes all comment groups
every identifier node maps to a 1-based line and 1-based column position via the token.FileSet
position line and column are strictly greater than zero
tests.pseudocode: for pkg := range genGoPackages() { fset, files, err := parseGoPackageWithComments(pkg); assert err == nil; for _, f := range files { assert len(f.Comments) >= 0; ast.Inspect(f, func(n ast.Node) bool { if id, ok := n.(*ast.Ident); ok { p := fset.Position(id.Pos()); assert p.Line >= 1 && p.Column >= 1 }; return true }) } }

tests.title: Reference scanner candidate traversal obeys .gitignore rules, hidden directory exclusions, and index filtering
given: a workspace with .gitignore ignoring 'build/', a hidden directory '.git/', and active files in 'src/'
tests.when: candidate files are traversed for reference scanning
then: files inside 'build/' are ignored
files inside '.git/' and hidden files are ignored
only tracked and non-ignored files are inspected
tests.pseudocode: candidates := findCandidateFiles(ws, "Run", mockIndex); for _, c := range candidates { assert !strings.HasPrefix(c, ".git/") && !strings.HasPrefix(c, "build/") }

tests.title: Reference scanner uses whole-word identifier boundaries for outline-supported languages
given: a Python file containing 'def run_all():', 'runner.run()', and 'runaway = 1'
tests.when: reference scanner searches for target name 'run'
then: 'runner.run()' is matched at identifier boundary
'run_all' and 'runaway' are rejected because they do not match word boundaries
tests.pseudocode: matches := scanFileForName("test.py", "run"); assert len(matches) == 1 && matches[0].LineText == "runner.run()"

tests.title: Reference scanner classifies code matches outside comments and strings in outline files as lexical
given: a TypeScript file declaring a caller 'service.execute()' with a known symbol table target 'execute'
tests.when: reference scanner inspects the code match outside strings and comments
then: ReferenceSite is created with Confidence set to 'lexical'
tests.pseudocode: site := scanNonGoSite("app.ts", "service.execute()", targetDecl); assert site.Confidence == "lexical"

tests.title: Reference scanner classifies matches inside comments, strings, or unparseable files as text
given: a Python file containing comment '# call execute here' and string '\"call execute\"' and an unsupported Markdown file with 'execute'
tests.when: reference scanner checks matches for known target 'execute'
then: the match inside the comment has Confidence set to 'text'
the match inside the string literal has Confidence set to 'text'
the match in the Markdown file has Confidence set to 'text'
tests.pseudocode: sites := scanAllSites("execute", targetDecl); for _, s := range sites { if isCommentOrString(s) || isMarkdown(s) { assert s.Confidence == "text" } }

tests.title: Reference scanner classifies all sites as text when target declaration is not in the symbol table
given: a workspace with Python, Go, and TypeScript files containing 'MY_GLOBAL_VAR' which is not in symbol table
tests.when: reference scanner executes for 'MY_GLOBAL_VAR'
then: every generated ReferenceSite across all files has Confidence set to 'text'
tests.pseudocode: sites := scanAllSites("MY_GLOBAL_VAR", outline.Decl{}); for _, s := range sites { assert s.Confidence == "text" }

tests.title: Reference match locator determines 1-based line number and 1-based byte column offset
given: arbitrary text file lines with indentation and UTF-8 characters
tests.when: for any reference match line, the match location is determined
then: the line number is 1-based (line >= 1)
the column offset is 1-based byte index of the identifier start (col >= 1)
the byte slice at line[col-1 : col-1+len(name)] equals the target name
tests.pseudocode: for match := range genMatchSites() { assert match.Line >= 1 && match.Column >= 1; line := getRawLine(match.Path, match.Line); assert line[match.Column-1:match.Column-1+len(targetName)] == targetName }

tests.title: Attribution engine inspects outline declarations spanning the site line
given: a file outline containing functions at lines 10-20, 25-35, and 40-50
tests.when: attribution engine looks up enclosing declaration for reference site at line 30
then: declarations at 10-20 and 40-50 are ignored
declaration at 25-35 spanning line 30 is identified as candidate enclosing declaration
tests.pseudocode: decls := []outline.Decl{{StartLine: 10, EndLine: 20}, {StartLine: 25, EndLine: 35}, {StartLine: 40, EndLine: 50}}; enc := findEnclosing(decls, 30); assert enc.StartLine == 25 && enc.EndLine == 35

tests.title: Attribution engine chooses innermost nested declaration with smallest line span
given: a file outline with outer class 'Engine' at lines 10-60 and inner method 'Start' at lines 20-30
tests.when: attribution engine resolves enclosing declaration for a reference site at line 25
then: both Engine (span 50) and Start (span 10) contain line 25
innermost declaration Start with smallest span 10 is assigned to ReferenceSite.Enclosing
tests.pseudocode: decls := []outline.Decl{{Name: "Engine", StartLine: 10, EndLine: 60}, {Name: "Start", StartLine: 20, EndLine: 30}}; enc := findEnclosing(decls, 25); assert enc.Name == "Start"

tests.title: Attribution engine assigns zero declaration with Kind 'file' for top-level reference sites
given: a file outline with a declaration starting at line 15, and a reference site at line 5 (top-level import or var)
tests.when: attribution engine resolves enclosing declaration for line 5
then: ReferenceSite.Enclosing is a zero outline.Decl with Kind set to 'file'
tests.pseudocode: decls := []outline.Decl{{Name: "Foo", StartLine: 15, EndLine: 25}}; enc := findEnclosing(decls, 5); assert enc.Kind == "file" && enc.Name == ""

tests.title: Attribution engine renders signature or '<Kind> <Name>' for declarations and '<file>' for top level
given: a declaration with signature 'func (r *Runner) Run() error', a declaration without signature 'class Controller', and a top-level file declaration
tests.when: enclosing declaration labels are rendered
then: the first renders as 'func (r *Runner) Run() error'
the second renders as 'class Controller'
the top-level declaration renders as '<file>'
tests.pseudocode: assert renderEnclosingLabel(declWithSig) == "func (r *Runner) Run() error"; assert renderEnclosingLabel(declWithoutSig) == "class Controller"; assert renderEnclosingLabel(fileDecl) == "<file>"

tests.title: Source line snippet extraction trims whitespace, caps at 200 bytes, and sanitizes control characters
given: arbitrary raw source lines containing whitespace, tabs, control characters (\x00-\x1F), and varying byte lengths
tests.when: for any reference site, the source line snippet is extracted and sanitized
then: leading and trailing whitespace is stripped
byte length of the resulting snippet does not exceed 200 bytes
no ASCII control characters (byte < 0x20, except space) exist in the output snippet
tests.pseudocode: for raw := range genRawLines() { snip := sanitizeSnippet(raw); assert !strings.HasPrefix(snip, " ") && !strings.HasSuffix(snip, " "); assert len([]byte(snip)) <= 200; for _, b := range []byte(snip) { assert b >= 0x20 || b >= 0x7F } }

tests.title: Reference ranker sorts sites deterministically by confidence tier, test status, path, line, and column
given: a list of unsorted ReferenceSite entries spanning resolved, lexical, and text confidences across test and non-test files
tests.when: reference ranker sorts the site list
then: all 'resolved' sites precede 'lexical' sites, which precede 'text' sites
within confidence tier, non-test files precede test files
within test status, files are sorted alphabetically by slash-separated path
within a file, sites are sorted by ascending line number, then ascending column
tests.pseudocode: sortReferenceSites(sites); for i := 0; i < len(sites)-1; i++ { assert siteOrderLess(sites[i], sites[i+1]) }

tests.title: Reference ranker excludes test files when include_tests is false
given: collected reference sites located in 'pkg/client.go', 'pkg/client_test.go', and 'test/helper.go'
tests.when: filterSites is invoked with includeTests = false
then: sites in 'pkg/client_test.go' and 'test/helper.go' are removed
only sites in 'pkg/client.go' remain
tests.pseudocode: filtered := filterTestSites(sites, false); for _, s := range filtered { assert !isTestFile(s.Path) }

tests.title: Reference ranker truncates sites to max_results and appends CapMarker
given: a result with 50 matching reference sites and max_results set to 20
tests.when: reference ranker applies limits
then: sites slice is truncated to length 20
Truncated field is set to true
CapMarker('references', 'max_results', 20, 100, 'narrow with path or kind') is appended to text output
tests.pseudocode: res := applyResultLimits(sites, 20); assert len(res.Sites) == 20 && res.Truncated; wantMarker := CapMarker("references", "max_results", 20, 100, "narrow with path or kind"); assert strings.Contains(res.MarkerText, wantMarker)

tests.title: Reference ranker halts traversal gracefully upon MaxFiles or MaxDuration bound and appends SymbolPartialMarker
given: a reference query configured with an expiring deadline or MaxFiles limit reached during traversal
tests.when: bounds check triggers during candidate processing
then: traversal halts gracefully without error
result returns sites collected before expiration
Partial field is set to true
SymbolPartialMarker is appended to text output
tests.pseudocode: res := executeWithShortTimeout(ctx, fr, "Run"); assert res.OK && res.Data.(ReferenceResult).Partial; assert strings.Contains(res.Text, SymbolPartialMarker())

tests.title: find_references clamps max_results between 1 and 100 with default 30
given: arbitrary integer input for max_results
tests.when: for any call with max_results unsupplied or less than or equal to 0, or exceeding 100
then: max_results <= 0 defaults to 30
max_results > 100 clamps to 100
max_results in 1..100 remains unchanged
tests.pseudocode: for val in genInts() { clamped := clampMaxResults(val); if val <= 0 { assert clamped == 30 } else if val > 100 { assert clamped == 100 } else { assert clamped == val } }

tests.title: Result renderer outputs header with declaration name, backend, counts, and partial advisory
given: reference query results with backend 'go/types', 5 references across 2 files, 1 text match, and Partial true
tests.when: renderResultText is called
then: first line format matches 'find_references <name>  (go/types, 5 references in 2 files; 1 text matches) [partial]'
name and backend are accurately reflected in header
tests.pseudocode: txt := renderResultText(res); firstLine := strings.Split(txt, "\n")[0]; assert strings.HasPrefix(firstLine, "find_references Run  (go/types, 5 references in 2 files; 1 text matches)") && strings.Contains(firstLine, "partial")

tests.title: Result renderer groups reference sites under relative file paths with padded indented lines
given: two reference sites in 'pkg/runner.go' at lines 12 and 45
tests.when: renderResultText is called
then: file path 'pkg/runner.go' appears as a header line
sites appear indented with format '  L<line>  <confidence>  <enclosing>  <source_line>'
enclosing declaration column is padded for alignment across lines in the group
tests.pseudocode: txt := renderResultText(res); assert strings.Contains(txt, "pkg/runner.go\n  L12  resolved  func Start() error      runner.Run()"); assert strings.Contains(txt, "  L45  resolved  func Stop()              runner.Run()")

tests.title: Result renderer appends truncation and partial markers on distinct lines at the conclusion of text
given: a result with Truncated true and Partial true
tests.when: renderResultText produces final output
then: truncation CapMarker appears on its own line after the file groups
SymbolPartialMarker appears on its own line after the file groups
markers are separated from site listings
tests.pseudocode: txt := renderResultText(truncatedPartialRes); lines := strings.Split(strings.TrimSpace(txt), "\n"); assert strings.Contains(lines[len(lines)-2], "cap=") || strings.Contains(lines[len(lines)-1], "cap="); assert strings.Contains(txt, SymbolPartialMarker())

tests.title: Result renderer populates ToolResult.Data with complete ReferenceResult structure
given: a completed reference resolution run
tests.when: ToolResult.Data is inspected
then: Data can be asserted as ReferenceResult
Target, Sites, Backend, Partial, Truncated, PackagesChecked, and Errors are populated with appropriate values
tests.pseudocode: data, ok := res.Data.(ReferenceResult); assert ok; assert data.Backend != ""; assert data.PackagesChecked >= 0 && data.Errors >= 0

tests.title: Result renderer returns successful ToolResult with zero references indicated when no matches exist
given: a workspace where no file contains the queried identifier
tests.when: find_references executes
then: ToolResult has OK true
Text indicates zero references found
Data contains an empty Sites slice (len == 0)
tests.pseudocode: res := fr.Execute(ctx, []byte(`{"name":"NeverUsed"}`)); assert res.OK; data := res.Data.(ReferenceResult); assert len(data.Sites) == 0; assert strings.Contains(res.Text, "0 references")

tests.title: Reference cache initializes lazily on first query and persists across subsequent queries
given: a newly created fileTools instance with no prior reference queries
tests.when: reference cache accessor is called on first query and second query
then: reference cache is nil before first query
reference cache is instantiated on first query
second query reuses the exact same reference cache instance in memory
tests.pseudocode: assert ft.refCache == nil; ft.getRefCache(); c1 := ft.refCache; assert c1 != nil; ft.getRefCache(); c2 := ft.refCache; assert c1 == c2

tests.title: write_file and edit_file mark the modified path dirty in reference cache upon lock release
given: an initialized reference cache containing cached file entries
tests.when: write_file or edit_file writes to 'pkg/service.go' and releases its path lock
then: reference cache has 'pkg/service.go' marked in its dirty set
package enclosing 'pkg/service.go' is marked for re-checking
tests.pseudocode: writeFileTool.Execute(ctx, writeArgs); assert refCache.isPathDirty("pkg/service.go"); editFileTool.Execute(ctx, editArgs); assert refCache.isPathDirty("pkg/service.go")

tests.title: Shell tools mark all cached packages and files for revalidation
given: an initialized reference cache with multiple cached packages
tests.when: execute, run_command, or powershell tool completes execution
then: reference cache has wholeTableRevalidate set to true
tests.pseudocode: execTool.Execute(ctx, execArgs); assert refCache.needsRevalidateAll()

tests.title: Reference query re-parses dirty Go packages, re-outlines dirty files, and purges deleted files
given: a cached Go package and Python file, where Go file was modified, Python file was re-saved, and an extra file was deleted
tests.when: a reference query runs with dirty flags pending
then: modified Go package is re-parsed and re-typechecked

deleted file is purged from cache
dirty flags are cleared

tests.title: Modifying .gitignore causes candidate file cache to revalidate on subsequent query

files inside 'ignored_dir/' are excluded from the candidate search

tests.title: Workspace exports ReferenceOptions, ReferenceSite, ReferenceResult types and References method

then: ReferenceOptions struct has Path, IncludeTests, MaxResults fields
ReferenceSite struct has Path, Line, Column, Confidence, Enclosing, Source fields
ReferenceResult struct has Target, Sites, Backend, Partial, PackagesChecked, Errors, Truncated fields
(*Workspace).References method accepts context.Context, outline.Decl, ReferenceOptions and returns (ReferenceResult, error)

tests.title: Workspace.References returns ReferenceResult matching find_references tool output with deterministic ranking
given: a workspace with Go and Python files and an identified target declaration

tests.title: Workspace.References returns non-nil error when path does not exist or is not a directory
given: a Workspace instance with non-existent path 'no_such_dir' and regular file 'main.go'
